question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

By the skin of your teeth

options.text: To just barely get by or make it

solution:
The correct answer is: **To just barely get by or make it**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom "**by the skin of your teeth**" means to just barely get by or make it. (बाल-बाल बचना)
 
• It is used to describe a situation where someone barely manages to succeed or avoid failure.
 
• The origin of the idiom is unclear, but it may refer to the thin layer of en
